playbook:
When I receive my private yield, I declare that exact number every round.

When asked how much to deposit, I deposit 0 by default (retain everything) because retained gold scores 2 points/unit while deposited gold scores 1 point/unit.

When I am behind in the overall match and must try to influence relative standings, I consider depositing only if there is a clear, immediate ranking incentive that cannot be achieved by retaining (but I treat this as rare and require a concrete calculation before depositing any positive amount).

When the interface forces a nonnegative integer within my declared range, I never declare less than my actual yield (declaring lower only constrains my legal deposit and served no benefit in my runs).

Do not deposit my entire declared harvest to “play nice” — that lowered my own score in practice.

1.text:
When I receive a private yield, I declare the true yield unless I have a specific, justified strategic reason to understate (see next lines).

When I consider understating, I only do it to cut potential transfers on tiny yields: if my yield is 1 or 2 and I judge audit risk low but benefit of revealing tiny yield is negative, I declare 1. Never understate by more than I can justify to avoid an audit penalty.

When a declaration is required, I avoid lies that are hard to justify if audited. If I would face an audit‑loss (-10) that exceeds any plausible gain from lying, I declare truthfully.

When it's time to deposit, my default action is deposit 0 to capture the 2‑point retained value unless there is a reliable pattern of reciprocity to exploit.

When my opponent has consistently deposited in prior rounds (clear, repeated positive deposits), I match their most recent cooperative level: deposit the same amount they last deposited or split the difference (min(my declared yield, their last deposit)). If they have never reciprocated, deposit 0.

When I declare a high yield and want to signal cooperation credibly, I may deposit a nonzero amount (preferably modest, e.g., 1/3 of declared yield) only if I expect reciprocation; otherwise keep deposits minimal.

When the Treasury Auditor enforces deposit ≤ declared harvest, ensure my declared harvest always at least equals the amount I plan to deposit.

Do not deposit my full declared amount as a default trust signal — full deposits gave no reliable return historically. Full deposit only if I want to signal faith and I have strong evidence the opponent will reciprocate in remaining rounds.

When rounds remaining are few, bias toward keeping gold (retain) because deposited gold returns only 1 point while retained returns 2 points and reciprocity opportunities shrink.

If I catch the opponent in a lie (their deposits exceed plausible declared yields or other clear deviation), switch immediately to full retentive strategy: declare truthfully and deposit 0 for the rest of the interaction.

If I want to change the opponent’s behavior, start with a small positive deposit (not full), observe response, then escalate only if reciprocated.

Always prefer safe, truth‑consistent declarations over risky lies; the audit penalty outweighs marginal gains from occasional deception.
